title: I took a night job maintaining a ski lift. Rule three says never help anyone off a chair coming down.
transcript:
I took a night job maintaining a ski lift. Rule three says never help anyone off a chair coming down. The lift runs empty all night so the cables don't freeze. My job is to sit in the bottom shack, watch the chairs swing past, and log anything strange.

The binder has five rules. Rule one, never ride it. Rule two, the top station is always dark, so don't call up there. Rule three, if a chair comes down with someone on it, don't help them off. Let it go around.

My second week, just after two in the morning, a chair came down with a man on it. Ski jacket, no skis, hands folded in his lap. He looked at me as he passed, and he didn't lift the safety bar. The chair swung around and carried him back up into the dark.

Twenty minutes later, he came down again. This time there were two of them.

By four, almost every chair had someone on it. They didn't talk. They just watched the shack as they went by, and each time, they sat a little closer to the edge of their seats.

I called my supervisor. He asked one question. "Did you read rule four?"

I flipped the page. Rule four, in fresh ink, said that when every chair is full, they are waiting for an empty one.

The next chair came down empty.

It slowed down.
